conventions: A relative clause that resumes its antecedent with a suffix on a preposition, where the ASV writes a preposition and a bare relative pronoun and no separate pronoun: the preposition takes the word written for its own relation and the relative and the suffix share the one relative pronoun, headed on the relative (ECC.5.19, 'to whom God hath given'). Do not mark the suffix unrepresented; rule 22's first sentence reaches an element the ASV leaves unwritten, and this one is written inside 'whom'.

A supplied English 'hath' or 'have' was placed by rule 43's count three different ways in this chapter and none of them is a split: on the possessive lamed at 5.16 ('what profit hath he'), on the possessive suffix of chalyo at 5.17 ('and hath sickness'), where no hayah and no preposition stands and the suffix carries no other English word, and as its own added unit at 5.4 ('he hath no pleasure in fools'), where the bet is already spent on 'in' and nothing else in the clause makes it possessive.

A repeated English preposition belongs to a written preposition whose scope spans the coordinated phrases (ECC.5.7, both 'in's to the one bet, the first waw left unrepresented). Where no preposition morpheme licenses the English word, the count runs the other way: at ECC.5.10 the first 'with' is the preposition the English verb needs to reach its bare object under rule 44, and the second, standing in a line whose verb the Hebrew gaps, was given to the noun it stands before under rules 33 and 34. That second placement is the chapter's one open call and is noted on its unit; the alternative folds it into the distant verb's discontinuous unit.
report: Read all 46 candidate groups and the whole dump end to end, including the eight added units the table cannot see. Every difference but one is licensed by the source or by what the ASV wrote: harbeh takes its own adverb each time (much 5.12/5.20, many 5.7, sore 5.17); the article split at 5.1 against 5.12 is rule 29's fronting test running both ways in one chapter (anarthrous rectum in 'the sacrifice of fools', indefinite rectum in 'the sleep of a laboring man'); the existential heads on its negation word in all four places (5.1, 5.4, 5.12, 5.14); meumah fuses with the negative at 5.14 and 5.15 alike under rule 35; and the comparative min holds 'is better than' whole at 5.1 only because no tob stands there, while at 5.5 the written tob takes 'Better is' and min a bare 'than'.

One genuine error, patched: ECC.5.19 'asher natan-lo' -> 'to whom God hath given'. The verse pass gave 'to' to the lamed, 'whom' to the relative, and marked the resumptive suffix unrepresented under rule 22's first sentence. Rule 22's closing paragraphs forbid exactly that: the suffix resumes the antecedent (3ms against ha-adam), and the ASV writes no pronoun besides 'whom', so the resumption is inside that word. The relative and the suffix now share one unit headed on the relative, while the preposition keeps the 'to' written for its own relation, exactly as rule 22 leaves 'stones' to its noun in 'a land whose stones are iron'. The corpus carries 42 aligned and 19 noncompositional relative-plus-suffix units of that shape and none where such a suffix stands unrepresented beside a written relative pronoun.

BSB disagreements: the 13 Td rows across nine verses are the documented convention difference and each was rechecked (5.14's article is silenced by the demonstrative under rule 41, 5.19's by the quantifier 'Every', 5.12's by the indefinite rectum under rule 29, the rest by an ASV that writes no 'the'). The three waws (5.7, 5.12, 5.14) are surplus-connective counts under rule 14; the four prepositions (5.12, 5.15, 5.18) and the 5.12 suffix on 'enennu' are recastings that leave them nothing under rules 40, 50 and 52. None of those is an error. The 5.19 suffix was the one real candidate and is now fixed; no edge was touched to improve the rate.

Left standing, each already carrying its own note: the two supplied 'with's of 5.10 (verb's valency preposition at rule 44, then the gapped line's noun at rules 33/34) against the one distributed bet of 5.7, since 5.7 has a written preposition whose scope spans both phrases and 5.10 has none; the 'whether ... or' count of 5.12 (each im takes the word written for it, the waw unrepresented under rule 14); the added coordinating 'and' of 5.18 beside an unrendered second asher; and the supplied 'hath' of 5.17 on the possessive suffix against the added 'he hath' of 5.4, where the bet is already spent on 'in fools'. Three of these are recorded in the conventions log.
